definition: The independent regulator of health and adult social care in England.
source: Health and Social Care Act 2008 (established the Care Quality Commission)

full_term: Department of Health and Social Care
definition: The UK government department responsible for health and adult social care policy in England.
source: GOV.UK — Department of Health and Social Care.

full_term: Department for Levelling Up, Housing and Communities
definition: UK government department from 2021-2024, succeeded by the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government (MHCLG). Co-funder with The National Lottery Community Fund of the Changing Futures Programme.
source: GOV.UK — Department for Levelling Up, Housing and Communities (renamed the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government in 2024).

definition: The senior officer each local authority must appoint (jointly with the Secretary of State) to lead its public health functions.
The UK government department responsible for welfare, pensions and employment support.
source: GOV.UK — Department for Work and Pensions.

definition: The statutory NHS body that plans and commissions health services for a defined area.
The statutory joint committee of an integrated care system that agrees a health-and-care strategy for the area, bringing the NHS and local partners together.
source: Health and Care Act 2022 (integrated care partnerships)

definition: A specialist domestic-abuse support worker for survivors at high risk of harm.
An employment model in which specialists are embedded in mental-health teams; the strongest-evidenced employment intervention for adults with severe mental illness.
source: Evidence-based supported employment (Centre for Mental Health).

definition: The statutory assessment of the current and future health and care needs of a local population, prepared for each area by the responsible local authority and its partner integrated care board — discharged locally through the Health and Wellbeing Board.
source: Local Government and Public Involvement in Health Act 2007, s.116

definition: The multi-agency forum for managing the highest-risk domestic abuse cases.
source: SafeLives — What is a MARAC? (SafeLives stewards the national MARAC model and holds the definition)

definition: The unitary local authority for the Middlesbrough area.
The publicly funded health system, created by the National Health Service Act 1946 (operational 5 July 1948) and now governed by the consolidating National Health Service Act 2006.
source: National Health Service Act 1946 (established the NHS; now consolidated in the NHS Act 2006)

full_term: National Institute for Health and Care Research
definition: The national funder of the Health Determinants Research Collaboration (HDRC) infrastructure.

full_term: Redcar and Cleveland Voluntary Development Agency
definition: The local infrastructure charity supporting voluntary and community groups across Redcar & Cleveland.
The unitary local authority for the Redcar and Cleveland area.

A Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government capital programme funding move-on accommodation for people who sleep rough or are at risk of doing so; a predecessor to later rough-sleeping programmes.
The unitary local authority for the Stockton-on-Tees area, in the Tees Valley.

full_term: Tees, Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust
definition: The specialist mental-health and learning-disability trust serving the Tees Valley.
source: National Health Service Act 2006, s.30 (NHS foundation trusts; originally the Health and Social Care (Community Health and Standards) Act 2003)

definition: The multi-agency statutory board that coordinates adult safeguarding across the Tees area.
The sub-regional combined authority covering the five Tees Valley boroughs (Middlesbrough, Redcar & Cleveland, Stockton-on-Tees, Hartlepool and Darlington), led by the Tees Valley Mayor.
source: Tees Valley Combined Authority Order 2016 (SI 2016/449), under the Local Democracy, Economic Development and Construction Act 2009

full_term: Voluntary, Community, Faith and Social Enterprise
aliases: voluntary, community, faith and social enterprise
definition: Voluntary, Community, Faith and Social Enterprise — the collective term for charities, community groups, faith organisations and social enterprises.
The unitary local authority for the Borough of Darlington in the Tees Valley.
The unitary local authority for the Borough of Hartlepool in the Tees Valley.
The sustainable-transport charity and custodian of the National Cycle Network; 'Sustrans' is short for 'sustainable transport'.
The rural community council for the Tees Valley, supporting rural communities and voluntary organisations.
The regional infrastructure body representing and supporting the voluntary, community and social enterprise sector across the North East.

full_term: National Association for Voluntary and Community Action
aliases: National Association for Voluntary and Community Action
definition: The national membership body for local infrastructure organisations supporting the voluntary and community sector in England.
The NHS foundation trust providing 999 emergency and patient-transport ambulance services across the North East, including South Tees.
source: North East Ambulance Service NHS Foundation Trust

definition: The national body that led the NHS in England and oversaw commissioning; its functions are being brought back into the Department of Health and Social Care following the March 2025 decision to abolish it.
The NHS bodies that commissioned most local health services from 2013; abolished in July 2022 and replaced by Integrated Care Boards (ICBs).
The principal public agency for conducting criminal prosecutions in England and Wales, established under the Prosecution of Offences Act 1985.
The national governing body for tennis in Great Britain.
The UK government department responsible for education and children's services in England.
Collective term for children and young people, commonly used in health, education and social-care services.
A framework of environmental, social and governance criteria used to assess an organisation's wider impact and responsible practice.
A body that supports, develops and represents the local voluntary and community sector (for example a council for voluntary service); RCVDA is the LIO for Redcar & Cleveland.
Charities, community groups and other not-for-profit organisations; the narrower predecessor term to VCSE (which also includes social enterprise).
The transfer of land or buildings from public ownership (usually a local authority) to a community or voluntary organisation, at less than market value, to secure community benefit.

full_term: Specific, Meaningful, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound, Evaluate, Re-adjust
aliases: Specific, Meaningful, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound, Evaluate, Re-adjust
definition: A goal-setting mnemonic extending the SMART objectives framework with 'Evaluate' and 'Re-adjust' stages.

full_term: Timely, Helpful, Respectful, Innovative, Values-based and Efficient
aliases: Timely, Helpful, Respectful, Innovative, Values-based and Efficient
definition: A values mnemonic describing how services aim to work. Distinct from the local Thrive Partnership.
A non-profit provider of social housing (typically a housing association) registered with, and regulated by, the social housing regulator.

Local arrangements to provide emergency accommodation for people sleeping rough during severe weather; a discretionary, non-statutory response prompted by cold-weather and other severe-weather thresholds.
source: MHCLG rough sleeping / cold weather provision guidance.

definition: A coordinated, person-centred approach bringing the relevant workers around one individual to plan and deliver joined-up support.
The coordinated management of a town centre's environment, economy and activity, usually as a partnership between the local authority, businesses and other stakeholders.
An umbrella term for a range of abuses disproportionately affecting women and girls, including domestic abuse, sexual violence, stalking and so-called honour-based abuse.
source: Home Office — Tackling Violence Against Women and Girls Strategy (2021).

definition: A geographical management area of Jobcentre Plus, the part of the Department for Work and Pensions that delivers working-age benefits and employment support.
source: Department for Work and Pensions — Jobcentre Plus.

term: Limited Capability for Work and Work-Related Activity
full_term: Limited Capability for Work and Work-Related Activity
aliases: Limited Capability for Work and Work-Related Activity
definition: A Universal Credit determination that a claimant's health condition or disability so limits them that they are not expected to work or prepare for work, attracting an additional UC element.
source: Welfare Reform Act 2012; Universal Credit Regulations 2013

definition: A non-means-tested benefit that helps with the extra costs of a long-term health condition or disability; it replaced Disability Living Allowance for working-age adults.
A quality standard for supported-employment services helping disabled people and those with health conditions into work.
The single means-tested working-age benefit that replaces six legacy benefits including Housing Benefit, Income Support and tax credits.
A registered mental-health nurse who supports people with mental-health needs in the community; now more often titled community mental-health nurse.

full_term: Children and Young People’s Improving Access to Psychological Therapies programme
aliases: Children and Young People’s Improving Access to Psychological Therapies programme
definition: An NHS England programme to transform children and young people's mental-health services by embedding evidence-based psychological therapies and outcome monitoring.

term: Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services
full_term: Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services
aliases: Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services
definition: NHS services that assess and treat children and young people with emotional, behavioural or mental-health difficulties.
An administrative code recording that a patient missed a booked appointment without notice; increasingly reframed as 'was not brought' for children.
An approach to public policy that systematically accounts for the health implications of decisions across all sectors, to improve health and reduce inequalities.
source: World Health Organization — Health in All Policies.

definition: A statutory local-authority committee bringing together the NHS, public health, adult social care and children's services to improve health and wellbeing and reduce inequalities.
source: Health and Social Care Act 2012, s.194

definition: A local executive group supporting the delivery of a Health and Wellbeing Board's priorities.
The framework used to assess, plan and coordinate care for people with more complex mental-health needs; now largely superseded by the Community Mental Health Framework.
source: Department of Health — Care Programme Approach.

definition: A statutory partnership of local 'responsible authorities' (police, local authority, fire, health and probation) that works to reduce crime, disorder and antisocial behaviour.
The statutory duty on relevant partners to co-operate in safeguarding and promoting the wellbeing of adults (and, for children, under separate provisions).
A statutory advocate who represents and supports a person who lacks capacity to make certain serious decisions and has no-one else appropriate to consult.
The Department for Education's statutory safeguarding guidance that schools and colleges in England must have regard to.
The former statutory body coordinating local safeguarding of children; replaced from 2019 by multi-agency safeguarding arrangements led by three safeguarding partners.
The statutory arrangements through which police, probation and prison services jointly assess and manage the risks posed by violent and sexual offenders.
The Act that provides the legal framework for making decisions on behalf of adults who lack the capacity to make particular decisions for themselves.
The Act governing the assessment, treatment and rights of people with a mental disorder, including detention ('sectioning') in hospital.

term: Mental Health Act Code of Practice
full_term: Mental Health Act Code of Practice
aliases: Mental Health Act Code of Practice
definition: The statutory guidance on how the Mental Health Act 1983 should be applied, which professionals must have regard to.
source: Department of Health (2015), under Mental Health Act 1983, s.118

definition: A person-centred, outcomes-focused approach to adult safeguarding that works with the person to achieve the outcomes they want. Distinct from My Sister's Place (also 'MSP').
source: Local Government Association / ADASS — Making Safeguarding Personal; reflected in Care Act 2014 statutory guidance.

definition: A multi-agency group that shares intelligence and coordinates action on the quality and safety of local health and care services.
source: NHS England — Quality Surveillance Group guidance.

definition: The statutory multi-agency board that oversees and coordinates adult safeguarding arrangements in a local area (locally, the Teeswide Safeguarding Adults Board).
A statutory review a Safeguarding Adults Board must arrange when an adult with care and support needs dies or is seriously harmed and abuse or neglect is suspected, to identify learning.
The recognised body responsible for governing and regulating a particular sport nationally.
The bodies that set standards for, accredit or regulate a profession or field of practice.
A group-based, participative approach to treatment in which the community itself is the primary therapeutic agent, used in mental-health, substance-use and offender settings.
source: Royal College of Psychiatrists — Community of Communities.

definition: A notice requiring a person or body to stop or take action about behaviour that is unreasonable and has a detrimental effect on the local community's quality of life. Distinct from Community Psychiatric Nurse (also 'CPN').
source: Anti-social Behaviour, Crime and Policing Act 2014, s.43
